e-21695.worked_solution:
Given a linear system $\mathbf{x}' = A \mathbf{x},$ where $A$ is an $n \times n$ matrix, a *fundamental matrix* $\Phi(t)$ of the system is an $n \times n$ matrix whose columns are linearly independent solutions of the system.

In our cases, we have a $2 \times 2$ system. We are also given that the two linearly independent solutions of the system are the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}(t) & =[\begin{aligned}4 \\ 0\end{aligned}]{e}^{5t}=[\begin{aligned}4{e}^{5t} \\ 0\end{aligned}] \\ {x}_{2}(t) & =[\begin{aligned}4t \\ 4\end{aligned}]{e}^{5t}=[\begin{aligned}4t{e}^{5t} \\ 4{e}^{5t}\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

 

Therefore, our fundamental could be written as

**Note:** The columns of $\Phi$ can be written in any order.

Given a linear system ${x}^{′}=Ax,$ where $A$ is an $n\times n$ matrix, a *fundamental matrix* $Φ(t)$ of the system is an $n\times n$ matrix whose columns are linearly independent solutions of the system.

In our case, we have a $2\times 2$ system. We are also given that the two linearly independent solutions of the system are the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}(t) & =[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 0\end{aligned}]{e}^{3t}=[\begin{aligned}2{e}^{3t} \\ 0\end{aligned}] \\ {x}_{2}(t) & =[\begin{aligned}2t \\ -1\end{aligned}]{e}^{3t}=[\begin{aligned}2t{e}^{3t} \\ -{e}^{3t}\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

 

Therefore, our fundamental could be written as

$$
Φ(t)=[\begin{aligned}2{e}^{3t} & 2t{e}^{3t} \\ 0 & -{e}^{3t}\end{aligned}].
$$

decision.explanation: Place the given solutions x₁(t) and x₂(t) as columns to obtain option e. Its determinant is e^{2t}(cos²(2t)+sin²(2t))=e^{2t}, which is nonzero for every t, so it is a fundamental matrix.

after.name: Question 2
after.problem:
$$
{x}^{′}=[\begin{aligned}1 & -2 \\ 2 & 1\end{aligned}]x,\,{x}_{1}(t)=[\begin{aligned}\operatorname{cos}⁡2t \\ \operatorname{sin}⁡2t\end{aligned}]{e}^{t},\,{x}_{2}(t)=[\begin{aligned}-\operatorname{sin}⁡2t \\ \operatorname{cos}⁡2t\end{aligned}]{e}^{t}
$$

Consider the system of linear ODEs and two of its linearly independent solutions ${x}_{1}$ and ${x}_{2},$ shown above. Which of the following is a fundamental matrix for the system?
after.worked_solution:
Given a linear system ${x}^{′}=Ax,$ where $A$ is an $n\times n$ matrix, a *fundamental matrix* $Φ(t)$ of the system is an $n\times n$ matrix whose columns are linearly independent solutions of the system.

In our case, we have a $2\times 2$ system. We are also given that the two linearly independent solutions of the system are the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}(t) & =[\begin{aligned}\operatorname{cos}⁡2t \\ \operatorname{sin}⁡2t\end{aligned}]{e}^{t}=[\begin{aligned}{e}^{t}\operatorname{cos}⁡2t \\ {e}^{t}\operatorname{sin}⁡2t\end{aligned}] \\ {x}_{2}(t) & =[\begin{aligned}-\operatorname{sin}⁡2t \\ \operatorname{cos}⁡2t\end{aligned}]{e}^{t}=[\begin{aligned}-{e}^{t}\operatorname{sin}⁡2t \\ {e}^{t}\operatorname{cos}⁡2t\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

 

Therefore, our fundamental could be written as

$$
Φ(t)=[\begin{aligned}{e}^{t}\operatorname{cos}⁡2t & -{e}^{t}\operatorname{sin}⁡2t \\ {e}^{t}\operatorname{sin}⁡2t & {e}^{t}\operatorname{cos}⁡2t\end{aligned}].

after.name: Question 3
after.problem:
$$
{x}^{′}=[\begin{aligned}-1 & -2 \\ 2 & -1\end{aligned}]x,\,{x}_{1}(t)=[\begin{aligned}\operatorname{cos}⁡2t \\ \operatorname{sin}⁡2t\end{aligned}]{e}^{-t},\,{x}_{2}(t)=[\begin{aligned}-\operatorname{sin}⁡2t \\ \operatorname{cos}⁡2t\end{aligned}]{e}^{-t}
$$

Consider the system of linear ODEs and two of its linearly independent solutions ${x}_{1}$ and ${x}_{2},$ shown above. Which of the following is a fundamental matrix for the system?
after.worked_solution:
Given a linear system ${x}^{′}=Ax,$ where $A$ is an $n\times n$ matrix, a *fundamental matrix* $Φ(t)$ of the system is an $n\times n$ matrix whose columns are linearly independent solutions of the system.

In our case, we have a $2\times 2$ system. We are also given that the two linearly independent solutions of the system are the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}(t) & =[\begin{aligned}\operatorname{cos}⁡2t \\ \operatorname{sin}⁡2t\end{aligned}]{e}^{-t}=[\begin{aligned}{e}^{-t}\operatorname{cos}⁡2t \\ {e}^{-t}\operatorname{sin}⁡2t\end{aligned}] \\ {x}_{2}(t) & =[\begin{aligned}-\operatorname{sin}⁡2t \\ \operatorname{cos}⁡2t\end{aligned}]{e}^{-t}=[\begin{aligned}-{e}^{-t}\operatorname{sin}⁡2t \\ {e}^{-t}\operatorname{cos}⁡2t\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

 

Therefore, our fundamental could be written as

$$
Φ(t)=[\begin{aligned}{e}^{-t}\operatorname{cos}⁡2t & -{e}^{-t}\operatorname{sin}⁡2t \\ {e}^{-t}\operatorname{sin}⁡2t & {e}^{-t}\operatorname{cos}⁡2t\end{aligned}].
$$

**Note:** The columns of $Φ$ can be written in any order.

content.worked_solution:
Given a linear system ${x}^{′}=Ax,$ where $A$ is an $n\times n$ matrix, a *fundamental matrix* $Φ(t)$ of the system is an $n\times n$ matrix whose columns are linearly independent solutions of the system.

In our case, we have a $2\times 2$ system. We are also given that the two linearly independent solutions of the system are the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}(t) & =[\begin{aligned}\operatorname{cos}⁡2t \\ \operatorname{sin}⁡2t\end{aligned}]{e}^{-t}=[\begin{aligned}{e}^{-t}\operatorname{cos}⁡2t \\ {e}^{-t}\operatorname{sin}⁡2t\end{aligned}] \\ {x}_{2}(t) & =[\begin{aligned}-\operatorname{sin}⁡2t \\ \operatorname{cos}⁡2t\end{aligned}]{e}^{-t}=[\begin{aligned}-{e}^{-t}\operatorname{sin}⁡2t \\ {e}^{-t}\operatorname{cos}⁡2t\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

 

Therefore, our fundamental could be written as

$$
Φ(t)=[\begin{aligned}{e}^{-t}\operatorname{cos}⁡2t & -{e}^{-t}\operatorname{sin}⁡2t \\ {e}^{-t}\operatorname{sin}⁡2t & {e}^{-t}\operatorname{cos}⁡2t\end{aligned}].
$$

**Note:** The columns of $Φ$ can be written in any order.

after.name: Question 4
after.problem:
$$
{x}^{′}=[\begin{aligned}-1 & 2 \\ 0 & -1\end{aligned}]x,\,{x}_{1}(t)=[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 0\end{aligned}]{e}^{-t},\,{x}_{2}(t)=[\begin{aligned}2t \\ 1\end{aligned}]{e}^{-t}
$$

Consider the system of linear ODEs and two of its linearly independent solutions ${x}_{1}$ and ${x}_{2},$ shown above. Which of the following is a fundamental matrix for the system?
after.worked_solution:
Given a linear system ${x}^{′}=Ax,$ where $A$ is an $n\times n$ matrix, a *fundamental matrix* $Φ(t)$ of the system is an $n\times n$ matrix whose columns are linearly independent solutions of the system.

In our case, we have a $2\times 2$ system. We are also given that the two linearly independent solutions of the system are the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}(t) & =[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 0\end{aligned}]{e}^{-t}=[\begin{aligned}2{e}^{-t} \\ 0\end{aligned}] \\ {x}_{2}(t) & =[\begin{aligned}2t \\ 1\end{aligned}]{e}^{-t}=[\begin{aligned}2t{e}^{-t} \\ {e}^{-t}\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

 

Therefore, our fundamental could be written as

$$
Φ(t)=[\begin{aligned}2{e}^{-t} & 2t{e}^{-t} \\ 0 & {e}^{-t}\end{aligned}].
$$

**Note:** The columns of $Φ$ can be written in any order.

Given a linear system ${x}^{′}=Ax,$ where $A$ is an $n\times n$ matrix, a *fundamental matrix* $Φ(t)$ of the system is an $n\times n$ matrix whose columns are linearly independent solutions of the system.

In our case, we have a $2\times 2$ system. We are also given that the two linearly independent solutions of the system are the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}(t) & =[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 0\end{aligned}]{e}^{-t}=[\begin{aligned}2{e}^{-t} \\ 0\end{aligned}] \\ {x}_{2}(t) & =[\begin{aligned}2t \\ 1\end{aligned}]{e}^{-t}=[\begin{aligned}2t{e}^{-t} \\ {e}^{-t}\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

 

Therefore, our fundamental could be written as

$$
Φ(t)=[\begin{aligned}2{e}^{-t} & 2t{e}^{-t} \\ 0 & {e}^{-t}\end{aligned}].
$$

**Note:** The columns of $Φ$ can be written in any order.

decision.explanation: Placing the given solutions x₁(t) and x₂(t) as columns gives option e. Its determinant is e^{4t}(cos²(5t)+sin²(5t))=e^{4t}, nonzero for every t, so it is a fundamental matrix.

after.name: Question 5
after.problem:
$$
{x}^{′}=[\begin{aligned}2 & -5 \\ 5 & 2\end{aligned}]x,\,{x}_{1}(t)=[\begin{aligned}\operatorname{cos}⁡5t \\ \operatorname{sin}⁡5t\end{aligned}]{e}^{2t},\,{x}_{2}(t)=[\begin{aligned}-\operatorname{sin}⁡5t \\ \operatorname{cos}⁡5t\end{aligned}]{e}^{2t}
$$

Consider the system of linear ODEs and two of its linearly independent solutions ${x}_{1}$ and ${x}_{2},$ shown above. Which of the following is a fundamental matrix for the system?
after.worked_solution:
Given a linear system ${x}^{′}=Ax,$ where $A$ is an $n\times n$ matrix, a *fundamental matrix* $Φ(t)$ of the system is an $n\times n$ matrix whose columns are linearly independent solutions of the system.

In our case, we have a $2\times 2$ system. We are also given that the two linearly independent solutions of the system are the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}(t) & =[\begin{aligned}\operatorname{cos}⁡5t \\ \operatorname{sin}⁡5t\end{aligned}]{e}^{2t}=[\begin{aligned}{e}^{2t}\operatorname{cos}⁡5t \\ {e}^{2t}\operatorname{sin}⁡5t\end{aligned}] \\ {x}_{2}(t) & =[\begin{aligned}-\operatorname{sin}⁡5t \\ \operatorname{cos}⁡5t\end{aligned}]{e}^{2t}=[\begin{aligned}-{e}^{2t}\operatorname{sin}⁡5t \\ {e}^{2t}\operatorname{cos}⁡5t\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

 

Therefore, our fundamental could be written as

$$
Φ(t)=[\begin{aligned}{e}^{2t}\operatorname{cos}⁡5t & -{e}^{2t}\operatorname{sin}⁡5t \\ {e}^{2t}\operatorname{sin}⁡5t & {e}^{2t}\operatorname{cos}⁡5t\end{aligned}].

content.worked_solution:
Given a linear system ${x}^{′}=Ax,$ where $A$ is an $n\times n$ matrix, a *fundamental matrix* $Φ(t)$ of the system is an $n\times n$ matrix whose columns are linearly independent solutions of the system.

In our case, we have a $2\times 2$ system. We are also given that the two linearly independent solutions of the system are the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}(t) & =[\begin{aligned}\operatorname{cos}⁡5t \\ \operatorname{sin}⁡5t\end{aligned}]{e}^{2t}=[\begin{aligned}{e}^{2t}\operatorname{cos}⁡5t \\ {e}^{2t}\operatorname{sin}⁡5t\end{aligned}] \\ {x}_{2}(t) & =[\begin{aligned}-\operatorname{sin}⁡5t \\ \operatorname{cos}⁡5t\end{aligned}]{e}^{2t}=[\begin{aligned}-{e}^{2t}\operatorname{sin}⁡5t \\ {e}^{2t}\operatorname{cos}⁡5t\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

 

Therefore, our fundamental could be written as

$$
Φ(t)=[\begin{aligned}{e}^{2t}\operatorname{cos}⁡5t & -{e}^{2t}\operatorname{sin}⁡5t \\ {e}^{2t}\operatorname{sin}⁡5t & {e}^{2t}\operatorname{cos}⁡5t\end{aligned}].
$$

**Note:** The columns of $Φ$ can be written in any order.
